newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Markets mark time amid U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Markets mark time amid U.S. rate fears.

text.p: Leading European shares opened weaker on Wednesday and currency trading marked time after renewed interest rate jitters in The U.S. put the brakes on Wall Street's recent surge.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed marginally down overnight, after falling nearly 40 points early in the session. The main London, Paris and Frankfurt indexes were all lower in early trading, with London further weakened by British inflation data.

The foreign exchange markets appeared moribund, with the dollar steady in early European trade around levels seen late on Tuesday. Dealers said talk of a possible U.S. Federal Reserve rate rise was completely dominating the proceedings.

This follows comments on Tuesday by an unnamed Fed official to Reuters that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a rise in the 5.0 percent discount rate. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on September 24 and while the market has changed its mind several times about the likelihood of a rate rise, it now believes one is definitely in the offing.

Traders said the market was wary because of the wild swings in sentiment of late and investors were not willing to commit cash until they saw some hard figures. "This really has stirred up a hornets nest," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "The big ticket is the talk of a discount rate rise and it's that which is spooking people."
Analysts said that if the discount rate was raised it would suggest that the trend of U.S. rates had decisively turned, with serious implications for investors.
On the London stock market, analysts said the rate hiatus would mean investors would be wary of pushing ahead very far.

Meanwhile, early data showed British retail sales rose one percent in August for a 4.4 percent annual rise -- much stronger than analysts had expected. Government bonds fell as hopes for a cut in interest rates faded and stocks also slipped a couple of points lower.
On the Paris bourse stocks were about six points down in early trade. Dealers said although the market was weaker on the U.S. rate worries, it was still well supported.
A main focus was the French budget -- due to be released at 1400 GMT -- which Paris hopes will underpin its drive to European monetary union by proving it can meet Maastricht standards on deficits.
Analysts said a warm market reception for the budget could pave the way for a French rate cut as early as Thursday.
In Frankfurt, German shares opened bourse trade slightly down and dealers said they expected little change, or perhaps a marginal weakening, in light volumes.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5147 marks and 110.25 yen. Against the mark it as the same late in Europe on Tuesday and at 110.35 on the yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 5.7 points at 3,966.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 5.79 at 2,075.07.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 0.67 at 2,627.41.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $382.80 an ounce against $383.55 at Tuesday's London close. Silver was easier at $5.05
